clue.text: It is more than likely he will play

definitions.meaning: describes something with better than even odds of happening
as a noun, a player expected to be picked for the side

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the noun: a sportsman who is a likely starter is called this in team-selection talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with better than even chances is likely; a player probably selected is called by the same word as a noun.

clue.text: Dished out about a quid for material

indicators.note: about puts one piece around the other

parts.note: to dish out money is to pay it, paid
a quid is a pound, and L is the abbreviation for pound (librum)

explanation.surface: Someone paying roughly a pound for some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately'; here it says PAID goes around L. Quid is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan twill cloth is a fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: Fascinated by eastern sorceress in Rose's home

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the home

parts.note: a rose grows in a flower bed
a witch is a sorceress

explanation.surface: Someone spellbound by an oriental enchantress at the home of a woman named Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a person; it is the flower, whose home is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fascinated means spellbound or enchanted, a synonym.

clue.text: Prime minister in favour of including union leader after small party uprising

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
uprising in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lab is the short form of Labour, a political party

indicators.note: including says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of union

explanation.surface: A premier backs union leadership after a minor party revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uprising' reads upwards. 'Small party' is the abbreviation of Labour. Arthur Balfour was British Prime Minister 1902-05.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour led the British government as Conservative premier in the early 1900s.

clue.text: It's heaven, but not out of this world!

definitions.text: It's heaven, but not out of this world!

parts.words: It's heaven, but not out of this world!
parts.note: a paradise that exists on this planet rather than in the afterlife, playing on 'out of this world' meaning wonderful

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of this world' usually means superb; here it is taken literally, a heaven found on our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A blissful place on Earth is a heaven that is worldly rather than celestial.

clue.text: Ab-boil festered whilst in Spanish port

indicators.note: a boil that has festered has turned bad and changed, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty boil goes septic while someone is staying in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'festered' rearranges the six letters of 'Ab-boil'; the hyphen is just surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Basque city on the Bay of Biscay is a major Spanish seaport.

clue.text: Be in search of the legacy

parts.note: a quest is a search

explanation.surface: A treasure hunt for an inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'of the' are only links joining the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy left in a will is a synonym.

clue.text: Lawyer loses his way at the fence

indicators.note: loses says letters are dropped from the lawyer

parts.note: a barrister is a lawyer who pleads in court
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A barrister gets lost and ends up at a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' gives ST (street), not a route; drop it from BARRISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a barricade or obstacle, a synonym.

clue.text: Only fellow on strike?

parts.note: the one man who has walked out, read as the person who differs from the rest of a group

explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' means out; the single man who is out is the one who does not fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who does not fit with the rest is the single member left over.

clue.text: A letter said to have been used in a positive declaration

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a vowel is one kind of letter of the alphabet, so the phrase gives 'a vowel'

explanation.surface: A grammar point about which letter appears in an emphatic statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'a vowel' sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An open, firm admission or statement of belief is a declaration made positively.

clue.text: Needed 24 sheets in a bright colour

indicators.note: in says the sheets are placed within the colour

parts.note: red is a bright colour
a quire is a measure of paper, traditionally 24 sheets

explanation.surface: An order for a quantity of brightly coloured paper.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is simply a number: a quire of paper is 24 (or 25) sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed is something called for or demanded, a synonym.

clue.text: Violet canine?

definitions.meaning: a dog's-tooth violet is a spring-flowering plant, the erythronium
a canine is a pointed tooth, and also something belonging to a dog, hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Violet' looks like a colour or a girl's name; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The flower erythronium is commonly called by this name, and a pointed eye-tooth literally is a dog's tooth.

clue.text: Part of hero I captured in the symphony

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A heroic theme captured in a piece of orchestral music.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'in', which is only a link word joining the hidden run to the definition; 'the symphony' alone defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Third Symphony is known by this Italian title meaning heroic.

clue.text: Apathy of student with crooked grey hat

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy student lounging in a battered grey hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' looks like 'dishonest' describing the student; it only signals the rearranged hat letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a sluggish lack of interest or energy, a synonym.

clue.text: It is not a heavy vessel, one anchored with a beacon

definitions.text: It is not a heavy vessel
definitions.meaning: a boat that is light rather than heavy
a moored boat carrying a warning lamp, used where a lighthouse cannot be built

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, light and ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a lamp warns shipping; read in two words, it is a craft that is not heavy.

clue.text: Rush to move to northern town

indicators.note: move says the letters shift position to form a new word

explanation.surface: Hurrying to relocate to a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges the letters of 'Rush to'. THURSO is a town on the far north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caithness town is the most northerly on the British mainland.

clue.text: A French river bore

parts.note: un is French for a
the Derwent is a river in England

explanation.surface: A tedious person from France by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person or a tidal wave; it is the past tense of bear, endured.
explanation.definitionFit: To have borne something is to have endured or suffered it.

clue.text: Arranged in rank of improved stock

definitions.meaning: sorted into order by level or quality
livestock crossed with a better breed is described this way

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a farming one: cattle crossed with a pure breed to improve the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Things sorted into levels have been classified; farm animals bred up from a pure-bred sire carry the same description.

clue.text: Jack would explain pardon

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
to solve is to explain

explanation.surface: A sailor offering to account for a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon is to forgive or acquit, a synonym.

clue.text: Mussolini hurried into the river in France

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Il Duce was Mussolini's title
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: Mussolini dashing into a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also means imprisonment, but here the definition is the Durance, a tributary of the Rhone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Durance is a tributary of the Rhone in south-east France.

clue.text: Canal bridge, one that, in France, goes by the channel

parts.note: a means one
que is French for that
a duct is a channel or pipe carrying fluid

explanation.surface: Describing a structure that carries water across a valley in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes by' is only the link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge carrying a canal or water course over a valley is the structure defined.

clue.text: Angry at university with drunk

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunken student loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and irritable is a synonym for angry here.

clue.text: One examining bed canopy

definitions.meaning: someone who checks or tries things out
a canopy over a four-poster bed is called by the same word

explanation.definitionFit: An examiner or trier is one who tests; the overhead hanging on an old bed shares the name.

clue.text: Literary star

parts.note: not a famous author but the little star-shaped mark used in printed text

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests a celebrated writer; it is the printed symbol, whose name comes from the Greek for little star.
explanation.definitionFit: The typographical mark shaped like a star is used in written and printed text.

clue.text: Set the tone and brought into harmony

definitions.meaning: pitched a piece of music in a particular key

explanation.definitionFit: A tune pitched in a set key has been tuned that way; things attuned to each other are in agreement.

clue.text: Male pupil to go down before one in the city

indicators.note: before places the pieces ahead of the final one

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
L stands for learner
to sink is to go down
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy pupil struggling before finally settling in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Finland is a city.

clue.text: Voracious journalist in a dull colour

indicators.note: in says the journalist sits within the colour

parts.note: grey is a dull colour
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A hungry newspaperman dressed in drab grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Voracious means having a huge appetite, a synonym.

clue.text: Clown not to return with energy for him

indicators.note: not says letters are to be left out of the clown

parts.note: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime

indicators.note: return means the word to is read backwards

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A clown is told not to come back but to put more energy in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes OT ('to' backwards, from 'return') from the end of the clown, and E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A French man's name stands for 'him', a male person referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: Name in the finish qualified

indicators.note: in says the name is placed inside the finish

parts.note: the end is the finish
a title is a name

explanation.surface: A name appears at the end of a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualified here means having the right or claim, a synonym.
